podcast.title: Cassette Distributor
podcast.body: A young musician from Aberdeen, Washington, Buzz Osborne was known for distributing homemade cassettes featuring his favorite punk songs, including tracks from indie bands, The Stooges, Bad Brains, and Black Flag, only to people he deemed "cool." These tapes are credited with changing the world of rock and roll forever. "Several years earlier, a young musician from the logging town of Aberdeen, Washington, named Buzz Osborne began giving out cassettes featuring his favorite punk songs, All Indie bands, TBI from the stuages, tracks from bad brains and black flag, and Buzz gave these tapes only to people he considered cool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Leader of The Melvins
podcast.body: Buzz Osborne led The Melvins, one of the groups featured on the crucial "Deep Six" compilation, representing some of the earliest sounds of grunge. "And one of the groups on the album was led by one of the people responsible for distributing those legendary homemade punk cassettes. It was Buzz Osborne and The Melons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Buzz Osborne's Recommendation to Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of The Melvins and a figure "idolized by Kurt Cobain," played a pivotal role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. Osborne recommended Dave for the open drummer slot after Scream broke up, directly leading to Dave's audition and subsequent entry into Nirvana. "But then Buzz Osborne of the Melvins, a guy idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended him for the open drummer slot with Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Connecting Dave Grohl to Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of the Seattle band The Melvins, played a crucial role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. When Grohl, a friend, called him desperate for a drumming gig, Osborne, aware of Nirvana's drummer issues, provided him with the phone number of Nirvana's bassist, directly leading to Grohl's audition and recruitment. "Now Buzz was in a Seattle band called The Melvins, and Dave was hoping that he knew of any openings for a drummer. Now it just so happens that one of Buzz's friends was having drummer issues. He gave Dave the bass player's phone number."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Audition and Joining (1990)
xref.body: After his previous band Scream disbanded, Dave Grohl was connected with Nirvana through Buzz Osborne of The Melvins. Grohl auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25, 1990, and secured the drumming position instantly, completing the lineup that would become one of the most successful rock bands of the 1990s. "He auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25th, 1990, and he got the gig instantly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

xref.title: Joining Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: A few months after recording his Harling Talks AD demos, Dave Grohl received a call to audition for Nirvana. Scream had broken up over "girlfriend troubles" while on tour, leaving Dave stranded in Los Angeles. Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, who was idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended Dave for the open drummer position. Dave flew to Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990, and after an informal audition, became a member of the band without any explicit invitation, simply because "they just didn't ask him to leave." "Dave packed his kit into a large cardboard box and boarded a flight for Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Entrance – A Desperate Call
xref.body: After his band Scream broke up mid-tour in September 1990, Dave Grohl was stranded in Los Angeles and desperate for a gig. He called his friend Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, hoping for news of drummer openings. Osborne gave Grohl Kurt Cobain's phone number, leading to an invitation to Seattle. Grohl packed his drums in a cardboard box and joined Nirvana. "So buzz gave Dave the bass player his phone number and Dave made the call and was invited to come on up Packed all his drums into a big cardboard box grabbed his only bag close and headed up the coast to join this weird little band called of course Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Grunge Sound
xref.body: The Melvins, led by Buzz Osborne from Aberdeen, Washington, were featured on the 1985 "Deep Six" compilation, contributing some of the earliest sounds of grunge, arguably the most important alternative sound of the 1990s. "That's some of the earliest sounds of grunge, arguably the most important alternative sound of the 1990s. And it started in the local Seattle Indy scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

xref.title: Influence on Seattle Scene
xref.body: Black Flag's hardcore punk tracks were included on cassettes distributed by Buzz Osborne in Aberdeen, Washington, influencing the emerging Seattle sound. In Seattle, it was not considered strange to be a fan of both Black Flag and Aerosmith simultaneously, leading to a unique hybrid sound. "Hardcore punk mixed easily with hard rock and Seattle. No one considered it strange to be both into black flag and air smith at the same time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influencing Kurt Cobain
xref.body: Buzz Osborne and The Melvins were highly influential in the burgeoning Seattle scene, notably to Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who was such a devoted fan that he would sometimes roadie for them without pay. "Nirvana, featuring of course Kurt Cobain, a stoner and former janitor who was such a big fan of the melvins that he's sometimes rowdy for them for free."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Potential Collaboration with Kurt Cobain
xref.body: Buzz Osborne of The Melvins was mentioned as a potential musician Kurt Cobain might have worked with on a solo project if he had lived. "Maybe people like, I don't know, Buzz A's, One of the Melvin's"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Speculation on Undied Life
xref.body: If Kurt had not died, it is speculated that he would have separated from Nirvana for a solo project with different musicians, possibly Buzz Osborne of the Melvins and Michael Stipe of R.E.M., with whom he had discussed working. This solo record would likely have had a more acoustic feel with string arrangements. "Well my guess would be that he would have separated himself from Nirvana for his next project using different musicians. Maybe people like, I don't know, Buzz A's, One of the Melvin's and most likely Michael Stipe of R.E.M."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
